audit_findings.title: TRA cash claim is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $38.675 million latest filed liability; $0.25 per diluted share, or 2.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A finite contractual cash claim either reduces the equity bridge or must be captured through forecast owner-earnings cash outflows.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the tax receivable agreement liability was approximately $43.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted bridge line is visible, but it is unresolved whether historical owner earnings already include TRA payments. Even treating the entire latest liability as an additional deduction reduces base value from $11.85 to about $11.60 per share and the 30%-MOS threshold by about $0.17 per share, which does not change the valuation conclusion. Deduction would double count any payments already embedded in OE.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile TRA payments in the cash-flow-based OE calculation, then either model the filed payment schedule of approximately $5.3 million annually for seven years plus $1.1 million in the final year or deduct only the portion not represented in OE.

audit_findings.title: Ontario exit contradicts the null perimeter ruling
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 Ontario operating earnings remain in the $129.0 million anchor even though that operation is absent from the forward perimeter; related exit cash flows and retirement costs may also affect OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For example, in November 2025, the province of Ontario, Canada enacted legislation banning automated speed enforcement cameras, which led to our Company exiting the province.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter error is demonstrated because Ontario exited after contributing during most of FY2025. The $9.4 million impairment does not remove its historical operating contribution. Materiality cannot be established from the record because Ontario revenue, margin, capital spending, working capital, and exit obligations are not isolated. For scale, all Canadian FY2025 revenue was $31.6 million, or 3.2% of consolidated revenue, and Canadian revenue declined $4.607 million year over year in the first half of 2026.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Ontario-only 2025 results and exit cash flows, restate FY2025 OE to the post-exit perimeter, and rerun all scenarios without changing other assumptions.

audit_findings.title: The major NYCDOT contract entered a different economic regime after the anchor year
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-anchor pricing, service credits, penalties, cybersecurity spending, subcontracting costs, capital needs, and working capital change sustainable OE and potentially the growth path.
audit_findings.evidence: The terms of the new contract are materially different than our prior contract with NYCDOT, including service level agreements, service credits, liquidated damages, cybersecurity, and subcontracting requirements.
audit_findings.explanation: The anchor-contract mismatch is demonstrated and concerns a customer representing 17.9% of FY2025 revenue and 18.8% of first-half 2026 revenue. First-half 2026 Government Solutions revenue rose $24.922 million while segment profit fell $7.524 million, but those segment totals do not isolate NYCDOT economics. Given the concentration and expressly material contract changes, the issue is reasonably capable of changing the valuation even though its direction and amount remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Build a contract-level comparison of 2025 and 2026 NYCDOT revenue, cash margin, installation economics, service credits, penalties, cybersecurity and subcontracting costs, receivables, and capital spending; normalize OE and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 includes a concentrated NYCDOT installation and product event
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring project profit may overstate anchor OE, while associated receivable growth, inventory use, installation assets, and capital expenditures may depress it; sustainable follow-on service economics belong in the forward perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: We installed 300 red-light cameras during the third and fourth quarters of 2025, which contributed approximately $38.4 million of revenue in fiscal year 2025, of which approximately $23.9 million was installation services revenue and approximately $14.5 million was product revenue.
audit_findings.explanation: The $38.4 million revenue event is demonstrated and equals 3.9% of FY2025 revenue, including $23.9 million of installation services and $14.5 million of product revenue. Its OE contribution cannot be established because project-specific costs, taxes, working capital, and capital spending are not disclosed. Those components can offset one another, so neither direction nor materiality can be concluded from revenue alone.
audit_findings.action: Trace the project through gross profit, operating expenses, taxes, receivables, inventory, installation assets, and cash capital expenditures; remove only the net nonrecurring OE effect and retain separately supported recurring service economics before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Operating credit-card rebates may have been swept into the non-operating-income purge
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.5 million of FY2025 pretax credit-card rebates
audit_findings.mechanism: If the portfolio-income purge removed operating volume rebates, the $129.0 million OE anchor excludes recurring transaction economics and understates operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase of approximately $4.2 million was primarily attributable to increases in volume rebates earned from total spend on credit card transactions due to increased tolling and travel activity as well as favorable impacts from fluctuations in foreign currency rates in the 2025 period.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved processing possibility, not a demonstrated error. The filing identifies $21.5 million of FY2025 rebates tied to purchasing-card spend, equal to 16.7% of the OE anchor, despite their presentation in other income. That scale is reasonably capable of materially increasing value if the full amount was mistakenly purged; no adjustment is warranted if the pipeline retained it.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the account-level portfolio-income purge, separate the $21.5 million rebate account from interest income and foreign-exchange items, and rerun after tax only if the rebates were removed.

audit_findings.title: Camera-site retirement obligations may not be fully represented in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.898 million latest filed ARO; $0.12 per diluted share, or 1.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unfunded restoration cash costs attached to existing systems would reduce the equity bridge unless expected settlements are already represented in forecast OE or capital spending.
audit_findings.evidence: Asset retirement obligations are contractual obligations to restore property to its initial state.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the obligation is omitted is unresolved: cash settlements can already enter OE when paid, while additions and accretion are noncash accounting entries. Even treating the entire latest ARO as an additional equity deduction reduces base value by only about $0.12 per share and the 30%-MOS threshold by about $0.08 per share, which does not change the valuation conclusion. FY2025 settlements were $0.950 million versus a $129.0 million OE anchor.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile ARO additions, accretion, capitalized restoration assets, and settlements to OE; deduct only obligations not already captured in forecast cash costs and confirm the immaterial conclusion with a bridge rerun.
